description: Add the ability to view, edit, and delete individual ledger transactions from the TUI. Currently transactions are permanent once committed -- there is no edit, delete, or undo capability anywhere in the system. This feature adds a transaction detail view, inline editing with confirmation, and soft-delete with an audit trail.
principles: Confirm Before Destroy - All destructive operations require explicit confirmation showing what will change
Audit Trail - Deleted transactions are soft-deleted (marked inactive) with a timestamp, not physically removed
Edit in Context - Transaction editing happens from the Ledger screen where the user is already viewing their data
Minimal Schema Changes - Prefer adding columns to the existing ledger table over creating new tables
Transfer Pair Awareness - Editing/deleting one side of a transfer pair warns about the other side

techStack.pattern: Query Object Pattern - extend LedgerWriter with update/delete operations

userStories.title: Add soft-delete column to ledger schema
acceptanceCriteria: schema.py adds 'deleted INTEGER DEFAULT 0' and 'deleted_date TEXT' columns to ledger table via ALTER TABLE IF NOT EXISTS (backward compatible)
SQLite backend initialization runs ALTER TABLE to add columns if they don't exist (handles existing databases)
All existing queries that read from ledger add 'WHERE deleted = 0' filter (or 'WHERE deleted IS NULL OR deleted = 0' for safety)
TransactionQuery.get_transactions() excludes deleted rows by default, with optional include_deleted=True parameter
Existing tests pass unchanged (new columns default to 0/NULL)
New test: verify deleted rows excluded from get_transactions(), included when include_deleted=True

userStories.title: Add transaction update and delete methods to LedgerWriter
acceptanceCriteria: LedgerWriter.update_transaction(tx_id, **kwargs) updates specified fields on a ledger row by id
Updatable fields: createddate, trans_type, buy, buy_curr, sell, sell_curr, fee, fee_curr, exchange, group, comment
LedgerWriter.soft_delete_transaction(tx_id) sets deleted=1 and deleted_date=now on a ledger row
LedgerWriter.restore_transaction(tx_id) sets deleted=0 and deleted_date=NULL
All methods validate that tx_id exists before operating
All methods return the updated row (or raise ValueError for missing tx_id)
Unit tests for update, soft-delete, restore, and missing tx_id error

userStories.title: Transaction detail modal from Ledger screen
acceptanceCriteria: Pressing Enter on a selected row in the Ledger DataTable opens a TransactionDetailModal
Modal displays all transaction fields in a readable layout (field name: value pairs)
Modal shows transaction ID, date, type, buy amount/currency, sell amount/currency, fee, wallet, group, comment
Modal has action buttons: [Edit] [Delete] [Close]
Close dismisses modal with no changes
Test: pressing Enter opens modal with correct transaction data

userStories.title: Edit Transaction modal
acceptanceCriteria: Clicking [Edit] in detail modal opens EditTransactionModal with pre-populated Input fields for all editable columns
Date field uses text input with format validation (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS)
Numeric fields (buy, sell, fee) use Input with Number validator
Currency fields use text input (short, uppercase)
Wallet/exchange field uses wallet Select dropdown (same pattern as Feature-10)
Trans_type field uses Select dropdown (Deposit, Withdrawal, Trade, Spend, Mining, Interest Income)
Shows diff preview: 'Changes: exchange Strike → Coinbase, buy 0.5 → 5.0'
Confirm button applies changes via LedgerWriter.update_transaction()
Cancel returns to detail modal without changes
Test: edit modal saves changes, diff preview shows correct fields

userStories.title: Delete Transaction with confirmation
acceptanceCriteria: Clicking [Delete] in detail modal opens confirmation dialog
Dialog shows full transaction summary and 'Are you sure?' prompt

If transaction is part of a transfer pair (matching withdrawal+deposit within 72hrs, similar amount), shows warning: 'This transaction appears to be part of a transfer pair. The matching [deposit/withdrawal] will NOT be automatically deleted.'
Confirm calls LedgerWriter.soft_delete_transaction() and closes both modals, returning to Ledger with refreshed data
Cancel returns to detail modal
Deleted transactions no longer appear in Ledger (filtered by default)
Test: delete removes row from visible ledger, soft-delete flag set in database

userStories.title: Show deleted transactions toggle in Ledger
acceptanceCriteria: Ledger screen filter panel gets a 'Show Deleted' checkbox (default: unchecked)
When checked, deleted transactions appear in the table with strikethrough or dim styling and a 'DELETED' indicator
Pressing Enter on a deleted transaction opens detail modal with [Restore] button instead of [Edit] [Delete]
Restore calls LedgerWriter.restore_transaction() and refreshes the table
Status bar shows: 'Showing X transactions (Y deleted hidden)' when toggle is off
Test: toggle shows/hides deleted rows, restore makes transaction visible again

high: Schema migration (adding columns) must handle existing databases gracefully - ALTER TABLE can fail if column already exists
Adding WHERE deleted=0 to all queries is a wide-reaching change - must audit every query that reads from ledger
Editing buy/sell amounts directly impacts balance calculations and tax reports - user must understand the downstream effects
medium: Soft-delete adds a column read to every query - negligible performance impact but must be indexed if databases are large
Transfer pair detection for delete warning is heuristic-based (amount + timing) - may produce false positives
low: Modal patterns well-established in Feature-9 (Import Wizard) and Feature-11 (Wallet Management)
LedgerWriter extension follows Query Object pattern from Feature-8
